item.title: S&P Subscription
item.description:
Management and Budget | Public Comment on Contract Awards | Notice In plain English (machine-written): The Office of Management and Budget is seeking public comment on a proposed up-to-$244,500 contract with S&P Global Market Intelligence, LLC, for a subscription to its U.S. macroeconomic forecasting services, model and economic database.

This is a notice that the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) is seeking comments from the public about the proposed contract below.

 

Contract Type:  Contract

Contractor: S&P Global Market Intelligence, LLC.              

Contractor Address: 55 Water Street, New York, NY, 10041

Scope of Services: Subscription to S&P Global Market Intelligence for U.S. macroeconomic forecasting services, access to their U.S. macro model, and use of their database of economic data to OMB at 255 Greenwich Street, New York, NY, 10007

Maximum Value: $244,500.00

item.title: Alternative Enforcement Program (AEP) - 5-Year Review - Notice of Intent to Request the Release of Funds - Updated
item.description:
Management and Budget | Special Materials | Notice In plain English (machine-written): The Office of Management and Budget gave notice that New York City plans to ask the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development on or about Oct. 19, 2026, to release $51,780,000 in Community Development Block Grant funds for the city's Alternative Enforcement Program over five years.

COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG)

ALTERNATIVE ENFORCEMENT PROGRAM (AEP) 5-YEAR REVIEW - 2026

NOTICE OF INTENT TO REQUEST RELEASE OF FUNDS (NOI RROF)

             

REQUEST FOR RELEASE OF FUNDS

On or about October 19, 2026, the City of New York (the City) anticipates submitting a request to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) for the release of $51,780,000 of Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) funds authorized under Title I of the Housing and Community Development Act of 1974, (PL 93-383), as amended, to undertake the Citys Alternative Enforcement Program citywide, for a period of five years.

The Alternative Enforcement Program (AEP) is intended to address the serious physical deterioration of the most distressed buildings in New York City. Through AEP, the NYC Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) can order the property owner to repair or replace building systems as well as to address violations. item.title: Public Notice of Availability and Notice of Public Hearing
item.description:
Management and Budget | Public Hearings and Meetings | Public Hearings | Hearing: 2026-10-08 In plain English (machine-written): The Office of Management and Budget will release a plan amendment on Sept. 14, 2026, for $86 million in reallocated federal Hurricane Ida disaster recovery funds and will hold a public hearing Oct. 8, 2026.

COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT PROGRAM - DISASTER RECOVERY

PUBLIC NOTICE OF AVAILABILITY

NOTICE OF A PUBLIC HEARING

 

TO ALL INTERESTED RESIDENTS, GROUPS, COMMUNITY BOARDS, AND AGENCIES:

On Monday, September 14, 2026, the City of New York will release a substantial amendment to its Community Development Block Grant-Disaster Recovery (CDBG-DR) Action Plan for Hurricane Ida Recovery. Through this amendment, the City will detail its proposed use of $86,000,000 in reallocated CDBG-DR funding provided through the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD).

To access the plan beginning September 14, 2026, please visit: https://www.nyc.gov/site/cdbgdr/hurricane-ida…
